question.summary: No channel is known to be additive for every tensor power below a chosen m at least three, then first become nonadditive at m copies.
question.importance: A delayed violation would show that testing one or two copies cannot certify an additive channel law. It would expose a new level of regularization in channel-output entropy.
question.unresolved: Construct a genuine delayed-onset example with m at least three, or prove that two-copy additivity forces all-copy additivity in the relevant setting.

sourceRefs.statedTitle: Channel that is additive for fewer than m tensor copies but violates additivity at the m-th copy

claims.title: Explicit self-channel violations expose a quantifier trap
claims.text: Derksen and Lovitz give self-channel two-copy violations for every p greater than one. This solves the literal m equals two wording, but not delayed onset at m at least three.

claims.title: Hastings violations already appear at two copies
claims.text: The random-channel counterexample to minimum-output-entropy additivity does not remain additive through lower nontrivial tensor powers.

decisions.rationale: Status assessed against the archived statement in the 2026-08-12 primary-source audit; the evidence ledger lists the results considered.

editorial.interpretation: The intended problem must require m at least three. Otherwise the one-copy equality is tautological and any self-channel two-copy violation answers it.
